videos.title: FIX Color Contrast – Accessibility in Web & UI Design
videos.why: Covers text contrast, then the rule for UI components at 3:57, with three fixes from 5:03 (add a border, add another signifier, consider context) and a real pass and fail from YouTube's own interface at 7:42.

videos.title: Making Games Better for Gamers with Colourblindness & Low Vision | Designing for Disability
videos.why: A clear, well-illustrated look at how games handle colour blindness and low vision; the lesson that carries straight over to interfaces is backing up colour with shape, pattern or text.

podcasts.why: A plain-language explainer of colour vision deficiency as a spectrum from dulled colours to shades of grey; useful background before you try the simulations in lab-cvd.

reads.title: Understanding SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (Level AA)
reads.why: The official explanation of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text, including what counts as large and the note that ratios are never rounded up, so 4.49:1 fails.

reads.title: Understanding SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (Level AA)
reads.why: The 3:1 rule for input borders, icons, focus indicators and the parts of charts; it is the rule that pale grey form fields, a favourite of AI-generated layouts, break most often.

reads.title: Contrast and Color Accessibility
reads.why: Walks through each WCAG contrast and colour requirement in plain English, with sample pairs sitting right at 4.5:1 that show how weak a bare pass can look.
